page.layout: One printed page (right half of the opening) with running head at top, text in one full-width block, a Greek and Latin verse stanza set in the text, and a catchword at the foot right. Left edge of the scan shows the outer strip of the facing page (margin notes, cut off), which is not transcribed. No notes in the right margin.

main_text.l: ut quicquid prosperè confecerint, aut fatis suis
& benignioris Fortunæ afflatui imputent, quod fecit
Timoleon, narrante Plutarcho, Αὐτῆ ἱερὸν ἱδρυσάμε-
νος, καὶ αὐτῇ θύσας ——. aut rursus & sæpissime, id
tanquam proprio Matre & suis ipsorum viribus con-
fectum gloriantur. Tales erant, uti videtur, hic
Chaldæi, quos minatur se Deus contra rebelles Is-
raelitas adducturum. Et talem planè Ajacem ad vi-
vum effingit Sophocles in Flagellif. ubi hortante
pa-tre ut velit pugnam inire Deorum auxilio confisus,
respondit, ὑβοκόμπως καὶ ἀφρόνως, superbe ac stulte.
Πάτερ, θεοῖς μὲν κἂν ὁ μηδὲν ὢν, ὁμῶ Κράτος κατάκτησαιτο, ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ δίκα Κείνων πεποιθα τωτ[?] ἐπισπάσειν κλέος.

page.notes: Each printed line of the right page begins with a small printed quotation mark („), which is not transcribed as text. Left edge of the scan: fragments of the facing page's margin notes, cut off by the gutter; these belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "τωτ" in the Greek verse line and "ὑχὶ" in the Zonora passage; "nummis" and "curavit" in the Comnenus sentence (the word after "accinctam" and the verb are hard to make out in the scan). The last line of the page ends with "loci," and the catchword "vc-" stands at the right below it; the next page continues the sentence.
